title: Chestnut trees, cork oaks and quartz: the substance of La Garde-Freinet
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: La Garde-Freinet is read as much through its botany and rock as through its old village. Chestnut trees, cork oaks, quartz and woodland paths give the sector its true texture.
content:
In the Maures, La Garde-Freinet is not only a chain of lanes. As soon as one moves a little away from the centre, the commune regains its deeper substance: woodland, slopes, quartz, chestnut groves, cork oaks and undergrowth scents.

Quartz and lean soils impose their presence

Stone is never a neutral background in this sector. It appears in banks, in the colour of the soils and in the way paths hold together. This geology gives La Garde-Freinet a roughness very different from the shoreline.

A woodland of chestnut trees and cork oaks

The plant cover is more than a simple Mediterranean pine zone. The presence of chestnut trees and cork oaks recalls a rural economy, older uses of the forest and another way of inhabiting the gulf from inland.

Walking here means reading the commune differently

Once attention is given to this substance, La Garde-Freinet stops being only a charming village. It becomes a commune of the massif, with its scents, shade, slopes and a real continuity between botany, geology and local culture.
